items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The other two, Henry Campbell and Nick something, were just pals of Ginger.

ctx.x: As Egypt was a protectorate of England, it was normal that there were many English familes of the Royal British Navy. We made the acquaintance of four soldiers; two of them played music in a military band and the other two were jazz fans.

A.J. Henderson, known as "Ginger" because of his red hair, played trumpet and Teddy Hill was a drummer. The other two, Henry Campbell and Nick something, were just pals of Ginger. Henry Campbell played tenor-sax. They loved our music. Ginger was not a jazz trumpet player but Teddy Hill was the best drummer in Egypt and we really enjoyed when he would come around and sit in with us. There were many bands in Europe and the U.S.A. that would have been happy to have him as a drummer. We invited Ginger to sit in also…

We also made friends with a couple of Egyptian military aviators and some coast guards officers. After we became well acquainted with the coast guards officers, they used to give us big pieces of hashish and told us how they got it. There was plenty of hashish smoking in Egypt. Women were not allowed in Egyptian bars of sidewalk cafes. But everywhere, but I never found out if there was a law against it or only a law against smuggling because these coast guard officers told us that whenever they caught someone…
